clue.text: Italian food is the finished article

parts.note: something finished is over and done with, past
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone declares that Italian food is the last word in cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is the general name for Italian dough dishes such as spaghetti and penne.

clue.text: How fast we run to pillar-box?

definitions.text: How fast we run to pillar-box?

parts.words: How fast we run to pillar-box?
parts.note: a dash to the mailbox to catch the collection is made with mail-related speed, an old phrase for great hurry

explanation.surface: A question about how quickly one sprints to catch the last collection.
explanation.walkthrough: A pillar-box is the British red street mailbox; hurrying to the post is literally a 'post' haste.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning with the utmost speed, originally the speed of a mail courier.

clue.text: Woman will overlook bill for varnish

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits above, looking over, the second

parts.note: she will contracts to she'll
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A woman is going to ignore an invoice for wood finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlook' looks like 'ignore' but in a down clue means sit on top of.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin dissolved in spirit and used as a wood finish.

clue.text: Opposed to contents of Asian Times

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the two words Asian Times, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A newspaper's stance is against what the Asian Times prints.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means against, hostile towards.

clue.text: But he helps out the rest of the week too

definitions.text: But he helps out the rest of the week too

parts.words: But he helps out the rest of the week too
parts.note: a helper named after one weekday who nevertheless works on all the others as well

explanation.surface: A remark about a tireless assistant who does not only work one day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Defoe's Robinson Crusoe, Crusoe names his servant after the day they met; the phrase now means any loyal general assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: A devoted servant or right-hand helper, from Crusoe's companion in Defoe's novel.

clue.text: Child's room is not even somewhere to learn in the winter

definitions.text: somewhere to learn in the winter

parts.note: a nursery is a room set aside for young children
something not level slopes

explanation.surface: A parent complains a kid's bedroom floor is uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winter' points to skiing season, not the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle beginner ski runs where novices learn in the snow season.

clue.text: Flower came up

explanation.surface: A bloom pushed up through the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A common garden bloom, and also the past tense of rise, as the sun did at dawn.

clue.text: Stooped to dig-need straightening

indicators.note: putting the jumbled letters of dig-need in order rearranges them

explanation.surface: Bending down to dig needs straightening the back afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straightening' rearranges DIGNEED; 'Stooped' here is condescended, not bent.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop to something is to condescend, lower oneself to do it.

clue.text: Make submission for grant

explanation.surface: Applying formally for funding money.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb means both give in and concede, as in conceding a point in debate.

clue.text: Lieutenant covered by complete protection

indicators.note: the officer's abbreviation is wrapped inside the word for complete

parts.note: sheer means utter, complete

explanation.surface: An officer is fully protected.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place or thing that gives cover from danger or weather.

clue.text: Thoroughly associating cause with development

parts.note: the root of something is its origin or cause
and joins one thing with another
a branch is an offshoot, an outgrowth

explanation.surface: A theorist links causes to how things develop, comprehensively.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely, sweeping away everything from the base to the outermost parts.

clue.text: Relief from soldiers' malice

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
spite is ill will, malice

explanation.surface: Being spared the soldiers' spite would be a welcome break.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or reprieve from something unpleasant.

clue.text: Keep left in brick-transporter

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the builder's carrier

parts.note: a hod is a trough on a pole for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A builder keeps one item left in the hod.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something is to retain or keep it.

clue.text: Jack or King East received not this card though?

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

indicators.note: the word or takes in the two letters, holding them inside

parts.note: K stands for king in cards
E is the compass point East

explanation.surface: A card player hoped East held a jack or king, but got something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the jack and king named earlier: this card is neither of them, a wild card outside the suits.
explanation.definitionFit: The extra wild card in a pack is not one of the court cards like jack or king.

clue.text: Girl is to finish about one

indicators.note: the word for finish goes around the letter for one

parts.note: to end is to finish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl is about to finish something.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in the author Blyton.

clue.text: There's nothing of the animal in him

definitions.text: There's nothing of the animal in him

parts.words: There's nothing of the animal in him
parts.note: describes a person who consumes no animal products at all, read as a gentle man without brutish instincts

explanation.surface: Praise for a mild man without any beastly nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats and uses no meat, dairy or other product from creatures.

clue.text: Guide I brought in to conspiracy

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the word for conspiracy

parts.note: a plot is a secret scheme

explanation.surface: A guide admits being dragged into a secret scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot steers ships into harbour, so guides them.

clue.text: Boss's assistant, commonly a girl, an African high-flier

parts.note: a secretary assists an executive
bird is British slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: The executive's assistant is commonly a young woman who flies high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests a career woman; it is a long-legged bird of prey from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall raptor of the African savanna, named for its quill-like crest.

clue.text: Poor road, so ran from the plant

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters of road, so ran are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A rough track leads somebody to flee from a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is a flowering plant named for Aaron's staff in Exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall flower such as mullein or goldenrod, named after a biblical staff that blossomed.

clue.text: Characters from Magdalen scorn such a gossip

indicators.note: the letters of Magdalen scorn are taken and rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: An Oxford college's mockery is the work of a rumour-spreader.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who spreads malicious rumours and slander about others.

clue.text: Red clarets drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of clarets are reeling about in disorder

explanation.surface: Red wines have been consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid bright shade of crimson.

clue.text: City's light interrupted by gas explosion

definitions.note: the definition carries 's, standing for is, linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: the word for light is broken open by the scrambled gas

parts.note: a glow is a soft light

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters of gas apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A city's lights flicker after a gas blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Scottish port on the Clyde.

clue.text: Family keeps money in tin

indicators.note: the container word holds the money letter inside it

parts.note: a can is a tin
L stands for pound, British money

explanation.surface: A family stashes cash in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is an extended family group, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Skip to take exercise in vehicle

indicators.note: the exercise letters go inside the word for vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone skips the gym to drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap or frolic about playfully.

clue.text: Seize a point, making a complaint

parts.note: to grip is to seize firmly
E is a compass point, East

explanation.surface: An arguer seizes on a point to air a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripe is a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Pub is to north of farm building

parts.note: a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub stands north of the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A large agricultural shed for storing crops or housing livestock.

clue.text: A substitute for sin

definitions.meaning: a deputy, as in a ...-president standing in for another
a moral failing or wicked habit

explanation.surface: One wrongdoing replaces another.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a deputy (as a prefix or noun) and an immoral habit.

clue.text: Almost obstruct united group of countries

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to block is to obstruct

explanation.surface: Nations nearly block a united alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter K from BLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance of nations acting together, like the former Soviet bloc.

clue.text: Tablet one takes on passenger seat

parts.note: a pill is a tablet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tablet before riding as a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear seat on a motorcycle for a rider behind the driver.

clue.text: Rest leg, damaged in race

indicators.note: a damaged thing is knocked out of shape, so the letters of rest leg are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner rests a leg injured during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Leger is a classic British flat horse race run at Doncaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous annual horse-racing event at Doncaster, oldest of the English Classics.

clue.text: Possible harm, going round different Yorkshire town

indicators.note: the scrambled harm goes around the word for different
possible hints that harm can take another arrangement of its letters

parts.note: other means different

explanation.surface: Possible harm circles a different Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges HARM to RHAM, which then goes round OTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in South Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: Subdued, we tucked into fish

indicators.note: the word we is placed inside the name of a fish

parts.note: cod is a sea fish

explanation.surface: We ate fish and felt subdued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating but means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowed means intimidated into submission.
